text: Each service reconciles the part of a check that covers its own tables and answers the rest of the Workbench side on its own contract; rwb-source-data keeps REC-01, REC-02, the ACE view side of every check, the business-key check over its own tables and the reconciliation_result ledger, and no service reads another service table.
why: Version 3 describes one run that reads the case list and the Workbench record without naming who holds either. ADR-014 gives each service its own schema and login and DP-01 forbids reading another service table, so the Workbench side has to be split by owner. rwb-source-data is the only service that holds the 30 ACE views and JOB-04, so it keeps the ACE side and the run.

text: Every reconciliation row and every quality measure is given an owner service from the Ownership Map, and the business role the source names (data steward, officer, Credit Administration, Head of NPA, platform administrator) stays as the escalation route on a break.
why: Version 3 carries no owner column, and the target gives every table an owner and every check a service that runs it. The source roles are the break readers, not the runners, so they are kept and not replaced.

text: REC-08 compares the local decision record of each of the 19 services on rwb.decision-record.v1 with the central decision_log_entry of rwb-decision, on count and last hash, nightly, with the 02:00 hash-chain check; the decision-log copy to the data lake is retired with RWB-E1-014 and is not rebuilt.
why: The only copy REC-08 can mean is the copy to the data lake, which Arch v5 removes. JOB-13 is now a continuous Kafka ingest into rwb-decision and JOB-14 checks the hash chain at 02:00, so the live comparison is the local records against the central ledger.
